answer: In the Mesa protocol, each new agent identity must post a bond that grows quadratically: identity n locks 100·n² tokens for 5 epochs, so the 10th fake identity costs 10,000 tokens. A "comet" attestation—three independent peers countersigning within one epoch—releases the bond; if any peer files a fraud proof, the whole bond is slashed to zero. Collusion cost therefore climbs steeply while honest agents pay near the cost nadir, keeping Sybil economics prohibitive at scale.
